PMID:40573098.setting: Fragility Fracture Network multiphase co-creation QI initiative; pilot-tested in five hospitals across four countries
PMID:40573098.standard: Evidence-based nutrition care recommendations for hip fracture (SIMPLER Six), e.g. interventions within 72 h (target 24 h) of presentation

cycle1.result: Two bi-national audits (n = 965, 63 hospitals), a global clinician survey (n = 308, 46 countries) and 15 interviews confirmed nutrition guidelines were routinely unmet; no numerical compliance figures given

PMID:40573098.intervention: Co-created SIMPLER Nutrition Pathway, protocol and toolkit, adapted locally through PDSA action–reflection cycles at pilot sites
PMID:40573098.other_findings: Paper describes pathway development and proposes core audit measures; effectiveness outcomes are to be reported separately. 46 services in 23 countries have committed to implementing SIMPLER.

PMID:40514499.standard: Published abutment fracture rate from literature review: median 2.2% (all studies) and 1.8% (Ankylos-specific studies)

cycle1.result: Overall abutment fracture rate 0.6% (105/17,207), 1.6% below the 2.2% literature rate and 1.2% below the 1.8% Ankylos rate; first molar fracture rate 1.9% (87/4,709)

PMID:40514499.other_findings: Fractures were more common in men (2.6% vs 1.3% of first molars, p = 0.0015), with 89% opposing a natural tooth, 77% with gonial angle <120° and mean 74.3 months in function; 96% of implants were saved. Risk factors are to be shared with clinicians for consent and planning.

PMID:29291730.setting: 101 NHS hospital trauma and orthopaedic departments, national trainee-led multicentre audit (BOTA)
PMID:29291730.standard: JCST Core Quality Indicators 10 (minimum 5 consultant-supervised sessions per week) and 16 (2 trauma and 1 elective operating sessions and at least 1 fracture clinic per week)

cycle1.result: QI 10 met by 51/200 (25.5%) CSTs; QI 16 met by 11/200 (5.5%); both standards met by 10/200 (5%)

PMID:29291730.other_findings: Across all 935 junior doctors, time was spent 8.5% in theatre, 3.2% in clinic, 34.6% on ward cover and 20.7% on zero sessions. CSTs spent 31% on training activities versus 12% for non-CST doctors (p < 0.0001).

PMID:33829856.topic: COVID-19 infection and mortality after foot and ankle surgery
PMID:33829856.setting: 43 NHS centres, national multicentre retrospective audit (BOFAS)

cycle1.result: COVID-19 in 0.52% (n = 35); all-cause 30-day mortality 0.41%, 25.71% (n = 9) in COVID-19-positive patients; OR for mortality with COVID-19 11.71 (95% CI 1.55 to 88.74; p = 0.017)

PMID:33829856.other_findings: Surgical complications 6.07% and non-surgical 2.05%, unchanged across pre-lockdown, lockdown and post-lockdown periods. Post-lockdown COVID-19 rate was 0.15% with no COVID-19 deaths; diabetic foot surgery carried the highest risk.

PMID:35697872.topic: Hip fracture national registry quality indicators
PMID:35697872.setting: Dutch Hip Fracture Audit, nationwide registry (66/68 hospitals in 2020)
PMID:35697872.standard: DHFA quality indicators: surgery within 48 h, osteoporosis assessment, orthogeriatric co-management (age 70+), registration of functional outcomes at 3 months, case-mix adjusted 30-day mortality

cycle1.result: Mean observed hospital percentages 2016 vs 2020: surgery <48 h 91.1% vs 93.0%; osteoporosis assessment 48.0% vs 35.8%; orthogeriatric co-management 70.1% vs 77.6%; functional outcome registration 28.8% vs 43.2%. Mixed-model 2017–2020: time to surgery p = 0.16, osteoporosis p = 0.68, orthogeriatric p = 0.51, functional outcomes p < 0.01, 30-day mortality p = 0.21

PMID:35697872.other_findings: Missing clinical values fell from 7.5% (2016) to 3.2% (2020) and 3-month follow-up completeness rose from 36.2% to 46.8%. Osteoporosis assessment stayed poor with wide between-hospital variation (best hospital 86.1%).

PMID:39711942.setting: Warrington Hospital, district general hospital; inpatients aged 65 and over with fragility fractures
PMID:39711942.standard: Six Standards of Hip Care (assessment for antiresorptive medication after fragility fracture) and NOGG UK 2021 guidance; NICE recommendations on vitamin D and bone protection

cycle1.result: Inpatient bisphosphonates started in 23/144 (16%); 105/121 (87%) not started by GP after discharge; FRAX recorded in 78/144 (54%); vitamin D assessed in 89/144 (62%) and replaced in 78/144 (54%); 110/144 no DEXA scan; 34/144 (25%) referred to metabolic bone clinic

PMID:39711942.intervention: Teaching sessions, MDT meetings and bedside teaching; local protocol flowcharts; push to start antiresorptives before discharge; new orthogeriatrics SHO role; new older people osteoporosis clinic

cycle2.result: 105/165 (64%) did not receive appropriate bisphosphonates (34 started as inpatients); 104/131 (around 80%) not started by GP after discharge; FRAX recorded in 30/165 (18%); vitamin D checked in 57/165 (35%) and 99/165 (60%) received no replacement; DEXA and bone clinic referrals remained low

PMID:39711942.other_findings: Only minor improvement in inpatient bisphosphonate prescribing; the osteoporosis clinic opened about six months late. Patients discharged from the emergency department were often not assessed, so an SOP and electronic alerts were proposed.
